summary.description: A white or colourless crystalline powder herbicide that can create explosive dust when mixed with air. Used to control germinating grasses and weeds, with declining use in recent years
environmental_impact: Deposits onto soil and water bodies from atmosphere
Can seep into groundwater despite low water solubility
Persists in soils and waters for considerable time
Found far from original point of release
Poses concerns at both local and global levels
Over-exposure may affect skin and blood in humans

top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: Simazine contaminates water systems by depositing from the atmosphere onto water bodies and seeping into groundwater. Its persistence in water environments for considerable time periods and ability to travel far from release points makes it a significant threat to clean water supplies and sanitation systems, affecting both surface and groundwater quality.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG15_Life_on_Land: As a herbicide, simazine directly impacts terrestrial ecosystems by controlling plant growth and affecting biodiversity. Its persistence in soils for extended periods and long-range transport capabilities mean it can affect terrestrial life far from application sites, disrupting natural plant communities and soil ecosystems essential for land-based biodiversity.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG2_Zero_Hunger: Simazine presents a complex relationship with food security - while it helps control weeds in agricultural systems potentially supporting crop yields, its persistence and contamination of soil and water resources poses long-term risks to sustainable agriculture. The declining use suggests concerns about balancing short-term agricultural benefits with long-term food system sustainability.
